title: Housing and Pay Protests Sweep Major Spanish Cities
paragraphs: Millions of Spanish workers shut down businesses and public transport on Wednesday, November 11 before thousands took to the streets of major cities in a nationwide protest.
The walkout — under the slogan "Salaries. Housing. Prices." — was the first general strike in Spain in 14 years, and the first ever in which the main reason was housing.

Housing activists said 400,000 marchers joined the protest in Barcelona. The city government also said that 55,000 people turned out just to walk behind one huge banner that read "Live. Not Just Survive."
Spanish government officials also estimated 120,000 people turned out in Madrid despite pouring rain.
Across Spain, average rents have more than doubled over the past decade, eating into household budgets and upsetting voters.

In Madrid, the average monthly cost of rent for a small apartment is around $1,300, while the national average monthly salary is around $2,700. That means the cost of renting an apartment in the Spanish capital is far more than the 30% of income recommended by housing experts.
Anger over rent increases recently reached boiling point after an 87-year-old woman named Maricarmen Abascal was evicted from an apartment where she'd lived for over 70 years.
Legal negotiations won Maricarmen the right to move back to her home, but she passed away shortly after.
Housing activists used the anger over Maricarmen's story to call for the strike, and soon won labor union support.

The housing activists want a number of measures introduced to protect renters, including the automatic renewal of leases. Meanwhile, unions demand more public housing and a new minimum wage agreement.

The protests were mostly peaceful. However, in Barcelona, some younger protesters were seen smashing the windows of brand-name stores and starting small fires on the Paseo de Gracia, a major shopping street. Some launched fireworks at police.
There were also some scuffles between protesters and police in Madrid. Police used pepper spray in some places and arrested 49 people for incidents related to the protests.
